topic: Passive with Verbs with Two Objects
task_instruction: Rewrite each active sentence in the passive voice. Use either object as the subject.
paragraphs: At the royal court, the steward prepares the great hall for an audience with the King and Queen. He welcomes the visitors with a respectful bow. {{red:The steward gives the King a list of the day's petitions.}} {{mask_1}} A page addresses the Queen formally. {{red:The page shows the Queen a map of the kingdom.}} {{mask_2}} The captain reports from the northern road. {{red:The captain has sent the royal council a message about the bridge.}} {{mask_3}} Before the doors open, the herald speaks to the gathered guests. {{red:The herald tells the guests a story about the founding of the castle.}} {{mask_4}}

The council considers requests from towns across the realm. {{red:The Queen offered the village a grant for its new well.}} {{mask_5}} The King reviews the proposal for the market square. {{red:The King will give the builders clear instructions tomorrow.}} {{mask_6}} The royal physician prepares a report for the Queen. {{red:The physician is bringing Her Majesty a report on the winter stores.}} {{mask_7}} A messenger arrives with news from the coast. {{red:The messenger has read the council a letter from the harbor master.}} {{mask_8}}

After the meeting, the royal household makes arrangements for a visiting ambassador. {{red:The Queen promised the ambassador a private audience.}} {{mask_9}} The steward arranges the guest rooms. {{red:The steward is offering the ambassador a room overlooking the gardens.}} {{mask_10}} The King speaks with the court tutor. {{red:The King taught the young prince a lesson in diplomacy last winter.}} {{mask_11}} The ambassador asks about the local customs. {{red:The court tutor will teach the visitors a traditional greeting.}} {{mask_12}}

The royal family then visits the castle library. {{red:The librarian lent the Queen a rare book about the realm's history.}} {{mask_13}} The Queen inspects a newly restored painting. {{red:The artist has shown the royal family the original colors beneath the old varnish.}} {{mask_14}} A musician performs in the gallery. {{red:The composer gave the princess a songbook for the midsummer feast.}} {{mask_15}} The steward checks that the guests are comfortable. {{red:The servants brought the visitors warm cloaks before sunset.}} {{mask_16}}

At the evening banquet, the King thanks those who served the court. {{red:The Queen gave each guest a small silver token.}} {{mask_17}} The royal treasurer presents an account of the year's work. {{red:The treasurer has given the council a detailed report on the royal farms.}} {{mask_18}} Before the guests depart, the herald makes one final announcement. {{red:The herald will tell the people the date of the spring festival.}} {{mask_19}} The King speaks kindly to the visiting musicians. {{red:The King offered the musicians a place at court for the winter.}} {{mask_20}} The guests bow and reply, "Thank you, Your Majesty," before leaving the hall.
